title: A Lent plan
hook: one prayer, one fast, one gift
tomorrow: what did the women do on the Saturday nobody talks about?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the long green season: grow slowly, first the blade, then the ear. Today the color changes to purple, and the plan gets short.

New Year's resolutions tend to come as lists: run, read, sleep more, save money, call Grandma. A few weeks later, the list is a guilt trip. Lent's plan is shorter. On Ash Wednesday, the Gospel at Mass is Jesus in Matthew six, naming three practices and asking that each be done in secret: giving alms, praying, fasting. Three things. That's the whole plan.
screen: `A LIST BECOMES A GUILT TRIP.` → `ASH WEDNESDAY, MATTHEW SIX.` → `THREE THINGS.`

segments.voice: Jesus doesn't argue for them; he assumes them. When you give alms, when you pray, when you fast. His point is how: quietly, for your Father who sees in secret, not for an audience. When you give, he says, don't let your left hand know what your right hand is doing. The book of Tobias, in the Catholic Bible, puts the three in one breath: "Prayer is good with fasting and alms." They hold each other up. The fast makes room, the room goes to prayer, and what you saved goes to someone else. So a Lent plan is one of each. One prayer: a set time, a psalm, a weekday Mass. One fast: something you'll go without, small enough to keep. One gift: money, time, attention for someone who needs it. Small enough that you could still be keeping all three on a tired Tuesday in week five. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: Lent's forty days echo Jesus's own forty days of fasting in the desert, in Matthew four. And this was a week of seasons, so here's the whole run: the door is wide, wait at home, keep feasting, the house blessed, grow slowly, and now, three things.
screen: `IN SECRET, NOT FOR AN AUDIENCE.` · `PRAYER IS GOOD WITH FASTING AND ALMS.` · `ONE PRAYER, ONE FAST, ONE GIFT.` · `A WEEK OF SEASONS.` · then, large: `THREE THINGS.`

segments.voice: Say your three things out loud, one short sentence each: one prayer, one fast, one gift. If any of them is too big to keep for weeks, shrink it and say it again. Then sit with the plan for the rest of the time, holding it the way you'd hold something easy to drop.
A Lent plan. One prayer, one fast, one gift, kept quietly through the forty days.
Your line: three things. Prayer is good with fasting and alms. See you next week.

chat.meaning: Lent's plan is three things that hold each other up: prayer, fasting and almsgiving. Small enough to keep, and done quietly.
